title: Comparative Spiritual and High-Writings Research
objective: Systematically study spiritual literature, religious/high writings, mythology, philosophy and related literary works to identify repeatable structures of knowledge formation, state transition, conflict, observation, transformation and self-organization.
research_question: Which structural patterns recur across independent textual traditions, which are tradition-specific, and which—if any—can be formalized into falsifiable hypotheses relevant to Gnozis?
non_goals: infer consciousness, sentience or panpsychism from textual similarity
convert philosophical interpretation directly into implementation
source_classes: classical and modern literature with explicit philosophical or spiritual structure
secondary scholarship used only with provenance and clear separation from primary claims
working_method: model entities, relations, transitions and information flows
compare only after preserving source-specific meaning
search actively for counterexamples and disanalogies
convert recurring patterns into explicit abstractions
formalize only when the abstraction is sufficiently precise
test against counterexamples and existing Gnozis semantics
classify the result as RESEARCH_ONLY, HYPOTHESIS, FORMALIZED, or ENGINEERING_CANDIDATE
candidate_structures: source -> model -> guide -> observer -> state transition
tension -> boundary encounter -> information acquisition -> transformation
local conflict -> accumulated contradiction -> model change

status_rules.RESEARCH_ONLY: descriptive or interpretive material with no formal engineering consequence
status_rules.HYPOTHESIS: explicit claim requiring counterexample or empirical/formal attack
status_rules.FORMALIZED: defined abstraction with stated assumptions and testable consequences
status_rules.ENGINEERING_CANDIDATE: formalized result mapped to a concrete architecture requirement but not yet accepted
status_rules.ACCEPTED_ENGINEERING: approved only after independent audit and evidence gate

core_boundary.rule: This research task may challenge or illuminate interpretations of existing architecture, but cannot create a second Core state model or change Core semantics by analogy.

migration_plan.phase_1: Create a provenance-aware corpus index and source records.
migration_plan.phase_2: Run source-by-source structural extraction using the fixed analysis levels.
migration_plan.phase_3: Build a cross-tradition pattern matrix with counterexamples.
migration_plan.phase_4: Promote only recurring, well-defined patterns to formal hypotheses.
migration_plan.phase_5: Attack hypotheses against Gnozis-Core invariants and adversarial cases.
migration_plan.phase_6: Create an engineering candidate only when a concrete capability or invariant is demonstrated.
migration_plan.phase_7: Independent review before any implementation migration.

migration_rule: No philosophical result migrates into Core because it is elegant, ancient, widespread or intuitively compelling. Migration requires explicit formalization, falsifiable consequences, architectural mapping, counterexample resistance and independent acceptance.

handoff.implementation_agent: Claude only after an accepted engineering task exists
